subject: Segura Health — connectivity, residency, and air-gap recap
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ingram <tom.ingram@segurahealth.com>, security@segurahealth.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Segura Health - connectivity, residency, and air-gap recap

Tom / Sec team,

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. If I've mischaracterized anything please flag it and I will correct.

Key pain points you shared:
- Regulatory requirement: PHI must remain in Segura's controlled VPC and not leave the region for retention or processing without explicit consent.
- Air-gap consideration: certain workloads (patient matching) will run in an isolated enclave with no outbound internet.
- Network constraints: strict egress controls, limited cross-VPC peering, and existing transit gateway policy that blocks public IP egress from managed services.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Validate that Redwood Private can be deployed into Segura's VPC or to an air-gapped subnet with on-prem adapter.
2) Identify minimal network changes to allow inference calls while preserving no-internet controls for isolated workloads.
3) Surface evidence (arch diagrams, SOC-like artifacts, and a summary SOW) for your security review and procurement.

Technical notes from the call (high level):
- Model hosting: prefer customer-managed hosting in your AWS account (account-level role + KMS).
- KMS/HSM: you require customer-managed KMS keys; HSM integration is an escalation item if required.
- Data flow: inference inputs must not be persisted outside the VPC; caching is acceptable only if keys and storage are under Segura control.

Deliverables Redwood will provide this week:
- A filled network checklist for your infra team (attached: segura_network_checklist.xlsx)
- A minimum VPC config PDF showing required subnets, route tables, and NAT patterns (attached: segura_minimum_vpc_config.pdf)
- A short diagram and blurb for security summarizing custody of PHI and KMS flow (Drive link below).

Immediate asks for Segura:
- Confirm whether the isolated enclave has a one-way transfer process (e.g., results that can be exported out to a secure S3) or must be fully air-gapped indefinitely.
- Share the current transit gateway policy or a short network contact for Jordan and me to loop into a technical review.
- Indicate procurement timeline and whether a SOC-2 evidence pack or an on-site audit will be requested.

Next steps and owners:
- Markus: deliver checklist + VPC sketch (today, done)
- Jordan: schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra team next week (ETA: Monday invite)
- Rachel: draft a short SOW + security summary for procurement (first draft EOD Tue)

Attachments: segura_network_checklist.xlsx (stub), segura_minimum_vpc_config.pdf (stub)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cSegura-qualification
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/54321/DEAL-2027-0543

Thanks — appreciate the clarity on the constraints.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Tom Ingram <tom.ingram@segurahealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: security@segurahealth.com, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segura Health - connectivity, residency, and air-gap recap

Markus,

Thank you for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side:
- The enclave is fully air-gapped for the patient matching workload. Nothing can leave that VPC except via a controlled export job that writes to a secure S3 in the same region (we can share the export spec).
- KMS: we can provide a customer-managed KMS key for encryption at rest; HSM would be a large ask and likely a roadmap item.
- Transit gateway: we'll share the policy doc. Our infra lead, Priya Rao, will be the primary contact for network-level changes (her alias is security@segurahealth.com).

Procurement: target is end of May for contract sign-off if the SOW and security artifacts look good. We may request a limited-time pilot in a dev VPC before a full rollout.

Can you confirm whether Redwood's Private offering can route outbound inference traffic to a private endpoint (no public IP) and whether your deployment supports placing outbound NAT in a controlled subnet?

Tom
Tom Ingram
VP Engineering, Segura Health
Tom.Ingram@segurahealth.com

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ingram <tom.ingram@segurahealth.com>, security@segurahealth.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segura Health - connectivity, residency, and air-gap recap

Tom / Priya,

Great notes — appreciate the specifics. Quick answers below and a proposed narrow set of changes that should keep the enclave compliant while enabling inference.

Answers:
- Private endpoints: yes. Redwood Private supports VPC Endpoints and can be configured to use a private interface endpoint (ENI) so no public IP is required on the inference hosts.
- NAT placement: we can recommend a pattern where only a small control plane subnet has egress to perform software updates and monitor health; inference traffic stays on private networks and never traverses public IP space. That can be locked down with route table and security group rules.

Proposed minimal changes (so you can present these to Priya):
1) Allow VPC Interface Endpoint from Redwood-managed role into a dedicated subnet (no public IPs).
2) Provide an IAM role with least privilege for the Redwood agent to create ENIs and write logs to a customer-controlled S3 bucket (with the KMS key you supply).
3) If air-gap is required for production: run a dedicated cluster inside the enclave with an outbound export job to secure S3 (we will not cache or persist PHI outside your KMS-protected bucket).

I'll attach one-page diagrams and try to keep the SOW narrow to avoid procurement drag. Jordan will follow up to schedule the tech session for next week — Jordan, can you share two 60-min slots Wednesday/Thursday?

Thanks,
-Markus

Attachments: segura_minimum_vpc_config.pdf (updated)
